part: PART 1 · BEFORE THERE WAS YOU
title: The Girl Before the Message
paragraphs: I have often wondered whether people can tell when someone is unhappy. Not the obvious kind. I mean the quieter kind, the kind that lives behind ordinary conversations, hides beneath laughter, and waits until nighttime to remind you that something inside your life is terribly wrong. I was not a girl who had forgotten how to smile. I laughed, worked, made plans. But I was tired. I was trying to hold on to a relationship that kept hurting me, and the harder I tried to make things right, the more I seemed to lose myself. I had become familiar with words that made me feel smaller than I was: that I was not good enough, that I complained too much. I carried those words into my confidence, my sleep, my thoughts about the future. I did not know that somewhere beyond this chapter a stranger would send me a message. I did not know how much my life could change after one ordinary hello.

part: PART 1 · BEFORE THERE WAS YOU
title: The Weight I Carried
paragraphs: There are things about that time I still struggle to put into words. I had fought for a relationship that was hurting me. I had taken risks, gone against my family's wishes, and endured painful consequences. My family did not approve of him, and the conflict around that relationship brought its own suffering. I was caught between fear, attachment, guilt, and a desperate hope that things might become different. My messages could be read, my friendships questioned, my choices controlled. I was expected to offer a transparency I did not receive in return. The strange thing about living under pressure is how ordinary it can begin to feel. You stop asking whether something is fair and start asking how to avoid the next argument. You become careful with every word. I wanted a life in which kindness did not feel conditional, in which honesty was not punished, and in which I could breathe without wondering what I had done wrong. More than anything, I wanted to feel like myself again.

part: PART 1 · BEFORE THERE WAS YOU
title: October Tenth
paragraphs: On the night of October 10, 2025, I prayed istikhara. I was tired of trying to understand something that kept hurting me. Tired of questioning my judgment and wondering whether the relationship I had fought for was right for me. There is a particular loneliness in not knowing which direction your life should take. You can ask others for advice; you can reason with yourself until every thought tangles with another. Eventually there are questions you carry somewhere deeper. So I turned to Allah. I asked for guidance, for clarity, for what was best for me, even if I was not ready to understand what that might look like. I did not know what the following day would bring. I cannot claim to know the unseen or the exact meaning of every event. But when I look back, the timing still takes my breath away. The night before I met you, I was asking Allah to show me a way forward. And the next day, there you were.

part: PART 1 · BEFORE THERE WAS YOU
title: A Girl Looking for Work
paragraphs: October 11 did not arrive looking like the beginning of a love story. There were no violins or dramatic skies, no beautiful stranger appearing in slow motion. I was looking for work. That was it. I was sitting there thinking about my future, trying to find something practical to do with it. Love was not on my agenda. The idea of developing feelings for a stranger would have sounded ridiculous to me. I was not someone who casually befriended men. I could be relaxed and friendly in professional conversations, but I took emotional boundaries seriously. I had no intention of changing that. And then, among the ordinary notifications of an ordinary day, came a message from you about a website. Sometimes I think the most extraordinary moments must find it amusing how completely ordinary they look when they first arrive. I was searching for work. You were looking for someone to build a cybersecurity website. At least, that was all either of us knew.

part: PART 2 · A STRANGER AT THE DOOR
title: The Notification
paragraphs: October 11, 2025. 4:20 PM. You entered my life with an Assalamualaikum. Not a rehearsed romantic line, not a compliment about my face. A respectful greeting, followed by a question: was I a developer or a designer? Were I doing freelance work? You needed a cybersecurity website. I was open to new projects. It made perfect professional sense. I wonder what you were thinking when you sent that message. Probably about the work, the design, the things that needed building. I doubt you were thinking about marriage. I certainly was not. If someone had whispered that the man asking about a website would become my husband, I would have laughed. But I replied, and you replied, and a story began moving without asking either of us if we were ready. The first thing I remember about our beginning is its ordinariness. The second is how grateful I have become for that one small notification.

part: PART 2 · A STRANGER AT THE DOOR
title: The Stranger Who Noticed
paragraphs: One of the first things you admired about me was something I had made. You noticed my LinkedIn banners, the designs and colour combinations, the way I tried to make things look beautiful. You told me I had a good eye and that you were excited to see what I would create for the project. At the time I simply thanked you and promised to do my best. Now I look back and find that detail tender. Before you knew my heart, you had noticed something in the way I saw the world. You were not trying to win me over. There was no pattern of flirtation, no hidden pressure, no performance. You were simply yourself: funny, lighthearted, respectful. And I was someone who did not usually make male friends, especially while committed to another person. Yet somehow our conversations began to feel like friendship. I made that friendship known rather than hiding it. I did not fully understand why talking to you felt so different. I only knew it did.

part: PART 2 · A STRANGER AT THE DOOR
title: The Sound of Something Lighter
paragraphs: I wish I could explain the exact quality of your presence in those first conversations. You did not arrive with answers to every problem in my life. My circumstances did not vanish because you entered them. But there was something about the way you spoke, something gentle in your tone and easy in your humour. You could be funny without being unkind. I noticed your respect toward me and toward other people. Your jokes made sense to me; my silliness made sense to you. For someone whose life had become so heavy, speaking to a person who was not adding more weight felt almost unfamiliar. Conversation did not feel like something I had to survive. I could just talk. I could laugh. I could be a little ridiculous. I would return to my day still smiling. You reminded me that life could be light, that I could be light, that perhaps I had not lost the happiest parts of myself after all. Perhaps they had simply been waiting for room to breathe.

part: PART 2 · A STRANGER AT THE DOOR
title: The Borders We Laughed About
paragraphs: I find it almost unbelievable now, looking back at the way we spoke about our countries. You were excited about Pakistan, so excited that you apologised for it. You said you wanted to visit at least once and told me I should come to Delhi too. At the time those were simply two friends talking about places. Pakistan. India. Delhi. Cities, roads, cultures, possibilities. Nothing more. Now I read those messages and want to reach into the past and tell those unsuspecting people something. One day these countries will not be casual topics of conversation. They will become part of the distance between your hearts. You will discuss borders not because you are curious about visiting somewhere, but because you are trying to find a place where you can finally belong together. The strangest part is that you were already imagining visiting my country before either of us knew we would fall in love. Perhaps it was coincidence. It is still one of my favourite coincidences.

part: PART 3 · SOMEWHERE BETWEEN LAUGHTER AND LOVE
title: The Girl Smiling at Her Phone
paragraphs: When we started talking on WhatsApp, something changed. Not dramatically, not all at once. I began smiling at my phone. Really smiling, the kind where someone could look at your face and wonder what was so amusing about a screen. We talked about everything and nothing. We could spend hours ranting about a reality show, becoming unnecessarily invested in people who did not even know we existed. I loved how ridiculous we could be, how an ordinary conversation could become hilarious, how we never seemed to run out of things to say. After about a week, I began noticing something else: I was waiting for your messages. I noticed when I wanted to tell you something. When something funny happened, my mind wandered toward sharing it with you. Somewhere along the way, without asking my permission, you had become part of my everyday happiness. I was beginning to look for you in the ordinary moments of my day.

part: PART 3 · SOMEWHERE BETWEEN LAUGHTER AND LOVE
title: The Morning of the Quail
paragraphs: There is a morning I will always associate with you. You had challenged me to wake up early, and somehow, without an alarm, I actually did. I had not carefully planned it. I simply woke up, and what I discovered made me grateful that I had. My male quail had injured my female quail with his beak. She was hurt, and I needed to care for her. I remember tending to her, trying to soothe her, and thinking about how differently the morning could have gone if I had slept longer. Then I told you what had happened. I told you I had accidentally woken because of your challenge, and if I had not, I might not have discovered her injuries in time. A silly challenge between friends had become connected to something that mattered. Perhaps this memory stays with me because it shows how quietly you were becoming woven into my life. Even an early morning and two little birds had somehow become part of our story.

part: PART 3 · SOMEWHERE BETWEEN LAUGHTER AND LOVE
title: The Laugh I Wish I Could Have Seen
paragraphs: And then there was the Bihari accent. If I ever needed proof that I had found someone who could appreciate my particular brand of ridiculousness, that moment would be enough. I changed my accent, being silly, and you laughed. Not a polite little laugh. You laughed so much that you had to leave your office. Then you told me you had not laughed like that in years. Years. I do not think you realised what those words meant to me. I knew what it felt like to carry things that made laughter difficult. The idea that I had given you even one moment of such unrestrained happiness made something inside me glow. I wanted to make you laugh again, not because I needed to entertain you, but because I loved knowing I could be a reason for that kind of joy. I was not only finding light in you. Somehow, I was becoming a little light in your life too.

part: PART 3 · SOMEWHERE BETWEEN LAUGHTER AND LOVE
title: The Heart Has Terrible Timing
paragraphs: I wish I could say falling for you happened at a convenient time. It did not. Our lives were still complicated. You were in a relationship whose future was uncertain because of family objections and caste differences. I was struggling to find my way out of a relationship that had taken too much of my peace. Neither of us had a simple road ahead. Feelings alone could not make difficult circumstances disappear, and I knew that. Yet I was beginning to feel them anyway. I had always believed loyalty mattered. I still did. I did not want to treat commitments carelessly or build happiness on dishonesty. So I faced questions I had never expected. What did these feelings mean? What would happen to our friendship? What if I was imagining something that was not there? And perhaps the most frightening question of all: what if you felt the same? Sometimes hope is scarier than rejection. Rejection gives you an answer. Hope asks you to imagine a future you might never get to have.

part: PART 3 · SOMEWHERE BETWEEN LAUGHTER AND LOVE
title: The Question I Could Not Take Back
paragraphs: Eventually I asked. I do not know where I found the courage. Perhaps I was tired of wondering, or my curiosity had grown stronger than my fear. I asked if you liked me. And you said no. Never. Certain words seem harmless until they land exactly where you are most vulnerable. I remember feeling embarrassed. I wished I could rewind the conversation and return to the version of myself who had not exposed what she was feeling. I apologised because I thought I had misunderstood everything: the jokes, the comfort, the ease between us. For a moment I wondered whether I had taken an ordinary friendship and complicated it with my imagination. It hurt more than I wanted to admit. Not because you owed me affection. You did not. But because I had begun hoping that the man who made my days brighter might be looking at me with the same quiet tenderness. And for those few moments, I thought I had been hoping alone.

part: PART 3 · SOMEWHERE BETWEEN LAUGHTER AND LOVE
title: The Truth Behind Your No
paragraphs: But the conversation did not end there. You told me the truth. You did like me. You had been afraid to admit it. Your existing relationship was unresolved, and although its future seemed uncertain, you did not know whether it would actually end. You did not want to step into something unfamiliar while everything else remained complicated. I understood your fear. I could not pretend the circumstances were simple, or that a confession automatically made everything right. But I remember the relief of discovering I had not imagined the feelings between us. You had not approached me with a plan. We had become friends without trying to become lovers, and then, quite inconveniently, our hearts had started asking for more. Your confession was not a rehearsed romantic speech. There was no grand declaration, just honesty, hesitation, and the complicated truth. I have never needed a perfect speech to remember that moment. I remember it because it was the first time I knew what I felt was not mine alone.

part: PART 4 · WHEN THE IMPOSSIBLE BEGAN TO CHANGE
title: The Space Between Wanting and Having
paragraphs: There is a difficult space between realising you love someone and knowing whether you can build a life with them. We lived in that space for a while. We could not wish away our circumstances. There were people involved, commitments to resolve, and histories that deserved honest endings. Neither of us knew what would happen. I think people forget that uncertainty when they hear a love story after it has worked out. They see the happy part, two people who finally get to call each other theirs. They do not see the fear of hoping too much, the difficult decisions, the possibility that the person you have begun imagining in your future might never be there. I was afraid of that possibility. By then you were not simply someone I enjoyed talking to. Your presence had become meaningful. I wanted us to have a real chance, something we could eventually stand behind with honesty and peace. Slowly, that possibility began to feel less impossible.

part: PART 4 · WHEN THE IMPOSSIBLE BEGAN TO CHANGE
title: The Past Finally Became the Past
paragraphs: Things changed. Not all at once, and not because love had made every problem disappear. But the relationships we had been struggling to move beyond eventually ended. Our former partners moved forward with their lives. For the first time the future between us was not only a beautiful, frightening question. It was something we could consider seriously. I remember how impossible that had once seemed, how easily everything could have remained unresolved, how many reasons there were to believe we had met at the wrong time. Yet the circumstances that had kept us uncertain were no longer holding us in the same way. I could allow myself to imagine what came next, not secretly or guiltily, not as a thought I had to push away. I could imagine you as the man I wanted to marry. It was a different happiness, quieter than the excitement of a confession, deeper than the thrill of receiving a message. It was the happiness of realising that something I had almost been afraid to hope for might become my life.

part: PART 4 · WHEN THE IMPOSSIBLE BEGAN TO CHANGE
title: The Man My Father Liked
paragraphs: I told my parents about you. Even writing that sentence makes me smile. I remember the girl I had been before you entered my life, whose relationship had become a source of conflict at home, who had been frightened and uncertain about her future. Now I was telling my family about someone I genuinely wanted to build that future with. Then you spoke to my father. And he liked you. My father liked the man I loved. It might sound simple to someone else, but to me it meant more than I can explain. There was comfort in knowing that the person I wanted beside me could also earn the respect of someone important in my life. You were no longer just a name in my phone. You were someone my family knew, someone I could imagine bringing into the everyday parts of my world. For a girl who had spent so much time feeling torn between love and family, that meant everything. For once I was not imagining a future in which I had to lose one to keep the other.

part: PART 4 · WHEN THE IMPOSSIBLE BEGAN TO CHANGE
title: Two Families, One Unfinished Dream
paragraphs: Then you told your family about me. And they liked me too. Suddenly this relationship that had begun in a LinkedIn inbox had reached the people who mattered most to us. Our families knew. They had begun to accept what we meant to each other. Something about that made our story feel beautifully real. There were still complications. You were Indian. I was Pakistani. We were separated by distance, borders, nationalities, and practical questions that affection alone could not answer. But we were no longer merely dreaming. We were thinking about how to make a life possible: a place where we could both settle, a country where we could build a secure future, a home where the distance between us would no longer be measured in thousands of kilometres. I know these things take time. Love does not replace paperwork, planning, or patience. But I know how it feels to have someone worth planning for. When I imagine that future, the first thing I see is not a country. It is you.

part: PART 5 · THE MAN BEHIND THE SCREEN
title: The Ketchup Situation
paragraphs: Every love story needs a conflict. Ours, apparently, involves ketchup. My love, I have tried to understand. I really have. But ketchup with an omelette? Ketchup with white sauce pasta? Ketchup with practically anything that has the misfortune of appearing on your plate? I remember telling you that I did not even like ketchup, not even poured over red sauce pasta. You told me you could barely eat anything without it. I asked, in disbelief, 'Anda bhi?' Even eggs? You, apparently, saw no problem. At this point I am convinced you would politely ask the world's greatest chef where the ketchup was kept. And the worst part? I find it adorable. I love that these tiny, ordinary things have become precious to me. I do not want only the impressive version of you, the handsome man in the photographs, the respectful husband. I want the entire human being, including the man who commits crimes against white sauce pasta. Perhaps marriage means disagreeing about something as ridiculous as ketchup and still wanting to share a dining table forever.

part: PART 5 · THE MAN BEHIND THE SCREEN
title: If I Could Describe Your Eyes
paragraphs: I wish you could see yourself through my eyes. I wonder whether you would understand why I sometimes look at your pictures longer than I intended. You are handsome. Ridiculously handsome. And your eyes. Oh, your eyes. There is something about them that makes me wish photographs could become real for a moment. I want to know what it feels like to have you looking directly at me without a camera between us. I wonder if I will be able to hold your gaze. After everything we have shared, I might still become terribly shy when we stand face-to-face. But what makes you beautiful to me goes far beyond your face. It is your gentleness, your respect for my family, the way you care for your parents and how deeply it hurts you when they are hurt. I know loyalty matters to you. I love that the person I find so physically beautiful is someone whose character I admire. You are handsome in ways a photograph will never capture.

part: PART 5 · THE MAN BEHIND THE SCREEN
title: The Kind of Love That Listens
paragraphs: There is something unexpectedly intimate about teaching someone how to cook through a phone. I know it sounds like the least romantic sentence in the world. But sometimes I ask you to make something for yourself, and you listen. I guide you through the steps. You follow them. Somewhere in that simple exchange I feel a tenderness I cannot explain. I cannot always be there to care for you. I cannot walk into your kitchen, make sure you have eaten, or stand beside you and complain about how you are doing something while secretly enjoying every second. But I can ask you to cook, and you do. Love lives in those small acts of consideration more often than people realise. In listening. In making an effort. In caring about another person's ordinary needs. I imagine you in our kitchen, me telling you that you are doing something wrong, you probably reaching for ketchup, and both of us laughing because this ridiculous little moment is exactly the life I wanted.

part: PART 5 · THE MAN BEHIND THE SCREEN
title: The Angel I Did Not Know to Ask For
paragraphs: Sometimes I think about the night before we met, about the girl who prayed for guidance because she did not know what to do with the pain she carried. Then I think about you, the stranger who appeared the following day, who made me laugh when life had begun to feel painfully heavy. I cannot tell you with certainty why Allah placed our paths together at that moment. But I can tell you what it feels like to me. It feels like mercy. Like light entering a room I had not realised had become so dark. Like discovering that the world still contained people whose gentleness was genuine. Sometimes I call you my angel, not because you are perfect or incapable of mistakes, but because your arrival felt like an answer to a question I was exhausted from asking. You did not erase my past or rescue me from every difficulty. You reminded me that a different kind of love could exist. When I look back at that October night and the year that followed, I whisper Alhamdulillah. For the timing. For the friendship. For you.

part: PART 6 · THE LOVE WE HAVE NOT HELD YET
title: One Video Call, A Thousand Feelings
paragraphs: There is something almost unbelievable about the fact that we have not met face-to-face. Not once. We have had one video call, one small window in which the distance between our faces felt less enormous. And yet here I am writing an entire book about you, about a love that has grown through messages, photographs, videos, laughter, uncertainty, and ordinary days. Sometimes I wonder how to explain loving someone so deeply when I have never held his hand. But intimacy is not always physical. Someone can become familiar to your heart long before he becomes familiar to your arms. I know the tenderness of your character, what makes you laugh, the people you love, and the habits that make me shake my head. Still, there is so much I have not discovered. I do not know what it feels like to sit beside you in silence or what your embrace feels like. I do not know how my heart will react when your voice is no longer coming through a speaker. And I want to know. Oh, my love, I want to know.

part: PART 6 · THE LOVE WE HAVE NOT HELD YET
title: I Will Be Wearing Yellow
paragraphs: I have thought about our first meeting more times than I can count. And I have decided something. I will wear yellow. You will wear black. I do not know when that day will come or where we will stand when we finally see each other. But I know what I want us to look like. Yellow and black, the colours of the happy ending I imagine, the kind of magic I loved in films and Beauty and the Beast. I keep trying to imagine what I will do when I see you. Will I freeze? Will I become so shy I forget how to speak? Will I cry before I have reached you? Or will I run into your arms and hold you so tightly you will have to remind me to breathe? I honestly do not know. I know I want a day with you, just us. No screens. No calls to disconnect. I want to look at you until looking at you no longer feels like something I have spent a year waiting to do. And when that first day ends, I want to know there will be another.

part: PART 6 · THE LOVE WE HAVE NOT HELD YET
title: The Life I Keep Imagining
paragraphs: When I imagine our future, I do not always imagine extraordinary things. Sometimes I imagine a kitchen, a quiet evening, you coming home tired, me asking whether you have eaten. I imagine laughing with you over something ridiculous. I imagine hearing your voice from another room and realising that, for once, I do not have to reach for my phone. I imagine disagreements and learning how to understand each other better. Days when life is difficult but we remember we are on the same side. I want to grow with you, into the people we are meant to become, while still recognising the two unlikely friends who spent whole days talking about a reality show. I want us to build a marriage where neither of us fears being honest, vulnerable, imperfect, or human. Forever is not merely a beautiful word. It is a thousand ordinary days. It is choosing kindness when frustrated, making room for each other's dreams, learning to love well as we change. I do not want a perfect life. I want a real one. With you.

part: PART 6 · THE LOVE WE HAVE NOT HELD YET
title: October Eleventh, Again
paragraphs: October 11, 2026. One year since a stranger sent me a message about a website. I think about the girl searching for work, carrying worries about her future, trying to find her way through a painful chapter. I think about the night before, when she prayed for guidance. I think about the respectful greeting that arrived the next day. I wish I could tell her: this conversation is going to matter. You are going to laugh more than you expect. You are going to ask a question that breaks your heart for a moment. You will discover he feels something too. You will tell your family about him. And one day you will write a book about a man you have not even held yet. My love, I wish there were words large enough to hold what I feel. I love you in the way I look forward to hearing from you, in the way I want to tell you every little thing, in the way I imagine you beside me when I think about the future. I pray we find a home where our nationalities no longer keep us apart. I want the distance to become a story we tell instead of something we endure. I want our first meeting to become a memory instead of a dream. I want the ordinary life with you, including the ketchup arguments. Happy first anniversary. We have lived a year of this story without a single embrace. Imagine how many chapters are waiting for us. The end of our first year. Not the end of our story.
